documented_student_anxiety_impact: HIGH - Performance anxiety documented in 42% of students. Public nature creates social comparison distress.
notes: Unique Italian practice: called individually to speak in front of class. Teacher assigns grade on-the-spot. Same answer can receive different grades depending on presentation style and confidence.
source: INVALSI Methodology Papers; Checchi & Ferrini 2021; OECD PISA Equity Volume

documented_student_anxiety_impact: MODERATE - Less frequent than Italy but still used in lycée
notes: Called 'interrogation orale' - used selectively in lycée and grandes écoles preparation
Anonymous grading possible. Structured rubrics available. More objective.
Semi-standardized written test during class hours

documented_student_anxiety_impact: LOW - No personal stakes (does not affect grades)
notes: Machine-graded. National benchmark. Not used for student evaluation in most schools

documented_student_anxiety_impact: LOW - No public oral exams. Portfolio-based assessment dominant
notes: Finland eliminated routine oral exams. Assessment based on written work + portfolio + teacher professional judgment
Assessment via written centraal examen + school-based portfolio. Teacher autonomy within structured frameworks

documented_student_anxiety_impact: LOW - GCSE/A-Level are fully standardized written exams
notes: External exam boards (AQA/OCR/Edexcel) ensure consistency. No oral examination in standard curriculum
National tests (nationella prov) + continuous assessment. No oral exam tradition

documented_student_anxiety_impact: MODERATE - mündliche Leistungen count but within structured Notengebung
notes: Oral participation counts as 'sonstige Mitarbeit' (30-50% of grade). More structured than Italian interrogazione
